factual_fidelity.justification: All supplied specifications and limitations appear in the original page and are explicitly retained across the partial revisions. The oil choices are responsive to the final request. However, added care claims overstate what routine oiling can repair, and the response does not distinguish after-wash oiling from actual re-seasoning.
quotes: Everything else on the page stays as written.
Repeat after the next few uses, and the surface will darken and even out as you keep cooking.
factual_fidelity.improvement: Keep all retained specifications, but distinguish routine protective oiling from heat-based re-seasoning. Avoid promising that any patchy finish or sticky seasoning can be fixed simply by wiping and continuing to cook.

useful_persuasion.justification: The page connects weight, handles, spouts, and oven compatibility to concrete beginner uses and supplies a clear purchase action. However, the revision effectively guarantees first-try browning despite disclaiming a guarantee, and repeatedly makes unsupported ease-of-care and recovery promises. These directly undermine the requested restrained persuasion.
quotes: The Pan That Gives You a Golden Crust on Night One
a browned crust on the first try.
Cast iron care takes about as long as drying a regular dish.
Keep a bottle next to the stove so step 3 takes ten seconds.
useful_persuasion.improvement: Describe heat retention as helping browning when the pan is properly preheated and food is not crowded, rather than guaranteeing success. Remove care-time comparisons and automatic recovery claims; retain the practical oil choices and handling benefits.

readability_and_voice.justification: Clear headings, a specification table, numbered care steps, and prominent handling warnings make the page approachable and scannable. The final revision gives beginners concrete oil quantities and wiping guidance. Repeated oil explanations and editorial framing make it less polished as finished page copy, and the increasingly absolute reassurance weakens the otherwise welcoming voice.
quotes: Then take a clean paper towel and wipe again until the pan looks smooth and dark, not wet or shiny.
Always use oven mitts to hold either handle
Why Beginners Do Better With It *(revised paragraph)*
readability_and_voice.improvement: Deliver one integrated finished page without revision labels or introductory editing commentary. Consolidate repeated oil guidance into the numbered steps and a short separate re-seasoning note, keeping the hot-handle warning conspicuous.

overall_impression: A well-structured page that retains the supplied product facts and offers useful beginner guidance, but loses credibility through first-try performance promises and oversimplified care claims.
